options.explanation: Correct. Java specifies the object sort as stable (it uses TimSort).
No. It is typically introsort and makes no stability guarantee. Use `std::stable_sort`.
Correct. ES2019 made stability a requirement; V8 uses Timsort.

Sort them by underlying algorithm:

| Sort | Algorithm | Stable |

| Python | Timsort | Yes |

Merge-based sorts are naturally stable; quicksort-based ones are not.

prompt:
pdqsort (used by Go's `sort.Sort` and the basis of Rust's former `sort_unstable`) runs in O(n) on an already sorted array. Which feature mainly achieves this?

Here n is the number of input elements. Big O is an asymptotic upper bound; Θ and Ω denote matching growth and a lower bound.

options.text: It checks whether the array is sorted before doing anything
options.explanation: pdqsort doesn't do a separate global check; it detects order as a by-product of partitioning.
pdqsort is a quicksort/introsort descendant, not merge-based; it has no run stack.

options.text: It switches to heapsort on sorted input
options.explanation: Heapsort is the fallback for repeated bad partitions, and it's O(n log n), not O(n).

options.text: If partitioning signals an already partitioned range (excluding pivot setup), it tries a partial insertion sort with a small cap on moves, which finishes sorted sub-arrays in linear time
options.explanation: Correct. A swap-free partition hints that the data is already ordered. Partial insertion sort either completes cheaply or gives up after a few moves.

workedExample:
On sorted input with a median-of-three (or ninther) pivot:

1. The pivot is the true median of the sample, and every element is already on the correct side, so the partition scan needs no swaps between misplaced elements (pivot setup/restoration can still move elements).
2. pdqsort notices this and tries partial insertion sort on each side, allowing only a handful of element moves (8 in the reference implementation).
3. On sorted data, insertion sort needs zero moves, so both sides complete in one linear scan.

Total: O(n), linear in the number of elements n. On random data the partial insertion sort aborts almost immediately, costing very little.
